spider_candidate_clusters.label: word / speech / name / sound as ordering interface
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Split cosmogenic speech, Logos ontology, sacred chant, Naam/Shabad, and naming philosophy; semantic similarity is not one mechanism.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Many traditions use information-like acts (speech, word, name, chant, distinction) as a bridge between undifferentiated reality and experienced order.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: sacred tree / axis / life structure
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Gita-Katha are not independent; Torah-New Testament are not independent; remaining cross-family similarity is symbolic, not causal evidence.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Tree imagery repeatedly models life, cosmos or connection between levels, but the graph does not establish a common historical source across all branches.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: moral accounting / judgment after or beyond ordinary life
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Near-Eastern textual contact and later lineage explain part of the cluster; Egyptian, Iranian and Abrahamic concepts are not interchangeable.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Moral behavior is repeatedly projected into a larger accounting horizon, but the mechanisms and metaphysics differ sharply.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: water/darkness/light/order in origin imagery
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Water, darkness and light are globally available human experiences; motif recurrence alone has low specificity.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Origin narratives often turn perceptual primitives such as darkness, water and light into models of transition from indeterminacy to order.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: restraint / mercy / compassion / non-hatred / justice
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Prosocial norms can converge because cooperative communities face recurrent coordination, violence and ego-control problems.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Very different traditions repeatedly promote regulation of aggression and ego through justice, compassion, restraint or nonviolence.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: death / renewal / resurrection / rebirth / liberation
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Resurrection, rebirth, funerary transformation, cosmic renewal and liberation are distinct ideas; density here is partly category inflation.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Mortality is a nearly universal pressure that generates multiple sacred models for continuity or transformation, not one shared doctrine.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: fire as sacred order / transformation
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: The Indo-Iranian historical relationship is a strong common-heritage explanation; multiple texts do not count as independent witnesses.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: Excellent lineage signal, poor independent-confirmation signal.

spider_candidate_clusters.label: mind / ego / desire / insight as the main battlefield
spider_candidate_clusters.topa_attack: Different traditions define self, desire and liberation differently; shared inward focus does not imply shared metaphysics.
spider_candidate_clusters.best_remaining_statement: A striking fraction of the corpus treats disciplined attention, desire or ego as a lever for changing lived reality.

topa_ranked_takeaways.why_interesting: It crosses several otherwise distant textual families and is structurally more specific than generic light/water symbolism.
Prosocial restraint appears through substantially different metaphysical systems.
Many corpora relocate the decisive struggle from external power to attention, desire, ego, wisdom or conduct.
Functionally similar moral-accounting structures recur, but historical contact and semantic non-equivalence remain major confounds.
